title: Northstar Labs - Redwood migration discovery (OpenAI -> Dedicated)
summary: Discovery call focused on migration from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated. Customer uses OpenAI for chat & embeddings, high token volumes for search ranking + chat, concerns on latency/cost and eval parity. Discussed Dedicated sizing, VPC/private options, vLLM/TGI compatibility, benchmarks, SOC2/KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: size Dedicated cluster, run benchmark plan, share security docs and pricing worksheet.
topics: Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO
action_items: Maya Chen — share Dedicated sizing worksheet and pricing deck — due 2026-08-26
Liam O'Connor — propose benchmark plan + example scripts (vLLM/TGI vs Redwood runtime) — due 2026-08-28
Carlos Mendez — provide 7-day sample traffic profile and top 10 prompts for eval parity — due 2026-08-27
Devon Li — share network constraints and VPC peering contact info — due 2026-08-27
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing & dedicated sizing worksheet
Schedule a 2-hour benchmark session (SE-led) against customer prompts
Share SOC2/ISO documents and KMS integration guide
Customer to confirm timeline and internal stakeholders for pilot
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:00:05] Carlos Mendez: Hey Maya, this is Carlos here, Carlos Mendez, Head of ML at Northstar.
[00:00:07] Anita Rao: Anita Rao, engineering manager.
[00:00:09] Devon Li: Devon, SRE.
[00:00:11] Jared Kim: Jared, CTO.
[00:00:13] Maya Chen: Awesome, and from our side Liam and Priya are on to dive into the technicals. Liam, want to intro?
[00:00:18] Liam O'Connor: Sure hi, Liam O'Connor, solutions engineer, I work on performance and deployments. we'll try to keep it focused on migration concerns and benchmarks.
[00:00:26] Priya Gupta: Priya here, sales eng, i'll help map requirements to config and security.
[00:00:30] Maya Chen: Great. quick agenda: understand current stack with OpenAI, pain points (cost/latency), target SLOs, and talk through Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private, then next steps. sound good?
[00:00:38] Carlos Mendez: yep. to kick off, we currently call OpenAI endpoints for chat and embeddings. monthly spend ~ $120k, peaks during business hours.
[00:00:47] Anita Rao: we're using embeddings heavily for semantic search + reranking, also some multi-turn chat for support assistant. latency is sort of okay at 300-500ms for chat, embeddings around 200ms but that spikes.
[00:00:57] Devon Li: reliability is our big worry, we see throttling and latency spikes during peaks. also cost unpredictability as usage grows.
[00:01:05] Jared Kim: top of page we want predictable per-token unit economics and better control over data residency.
[00:01:11] Maya Chen: Understood. when you say throttling, is that rate limit errors or degraded perf?
[00:01:15] Devon Li: both. sometimes 429s and sometimes requests just take 2-3s. our SLO target is p95 latency < 350ms for chat and embeddings < 250ms, and we want better consistency.
[00:01:26] Liam O'Connor: that helps, thanks. do you run any self-hosted inference today like vLLM or TGI?
[00:01:31] Carlos Mendez: we've run vLLM experiments in staging, but not in prod. performance was promising but ops overhead was high, memory fragmentation and OOMs when we scaled.
[00:01:40] Anita Rao: also compatibility was a pain—some behavior differences in tokenization and generation compared to OpenAI, so eval parity was not perfect.
[00:01:47] Priya Gupta: got it. a big part of migration is ensuring eval parity—customers usually run a short eval suite with top prompts to compare quality across models. we can help with that.
[00:01:55] Carlos Mendez: yes we have a set of 10 scoring prompts, we'll share.
[00:01:58] Liam O'Connor: good, that will help. on the Dedicated side: Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, you get a private tenant and can run within a customer VPC via our Private option. does data residency need to be in a specific region?
[00:02:12] Jared Kim: EU for some customers, but primary is us-east-1 for now.
[00:02:16] Maya Chen: we support region pinning and can provision Dedicated capacity in your chosen region. for VPC, we do VPC peering and private control plane if you go full Private.
[00:02:25] Devon Li: network-wise we'll need details—firewall rules and peering, also KMS integration for keys. does Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
[00:02:33] Priya Gupta: yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys for Private deployments. we can share the KMS guide.
[00:02:40] Anita Rao: what about SOC2 / audit logs? we do security reviews for any provider we put into prod.
[00:02:45] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we provide audit logs and model-level access logs for Dedicated and Private. we'll send the security pack.
[00:02:52] Carlos Mendez: great. switching to perf: Liam, how does our runtime compare to vLLM/TGI? we've seen vLLM be fast single-GPU in some cases.
[00:03:00] Liam O'Connor: short answer: we optimize across batching, KV cache reuse, custom attention kernels and quantization-friendly execution. in many multi-tenant/high-throughput workloads we outperform raw vLLM because we handle batching and routing more efficiently. but for single-request low-latency microbenchmarks vLLM can look good.
[00:03:18] Carlos Mendez: interesting. what about compatibility with models trained/served via OpenAI? tokenization and logits matching?
[00:03:24] Priya Gupta: there are subtle differences between infra implementations; we aim for generation parity with curated model variants and can surface model compatibility notes. part of the pilot is running your eval set to measure quality drift; if needed we can recommend alternative model checkpoints or prompt adjustments.
[00:03:38] Anita Rao: can you run our prompts and give delta scores vs OpenAI?
[00:03:42] Liam O'Connor: yes that's the benchmark plan we propose: a 2-hour SE-led run where we replay 7 days of traffic (or a representative sample) and score outputs against your golden set. we'll collect latency, p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and quality deltas.
[00:03:56] Devon Li: about costs—do you have a sense of unit economics compared to OpenAI? our spend is high so even a 20-30% reduction matters.
[00:04:04] Maya Chen: typically Dedicated reduces per-token unit costs substantially, but it depends on utilization. our Optimize tool can recommend batching and quantization settings to hit targets. we can model a pricing scenario in the sizing worksheet.
[00:04:15] Carlos Mendez: what about burst handling? we have spikes up to 3x baseline.
[00:04:19] Priya Gupta: Dedicated offers configurable autoscale and burst capacity options; for critical traffic we can provision headroom or fallback routing to a hosted pool if needed.
[00:04:27] Jared Kim: fallback to hosted—does that mean customer data leaves our VPC?
[00:04:31] Liam O'Connor: good question; fallback can be against a Redwood-hosted model that is regionally isolated, but we can discuss contract terms for data handling. for strict data residency you would keep traffic on Private.
[00:04:43] Anita Rao: any gotchas with running embeddings at scale? our embeddings are called synchronously from many services.
[00:04:48] Liam O'Connor: embeddings do benefit from batching; for synchronous calls we do continuous batching to keep latency low while increasing GPU utilization. we also expose async endpoints if you want to decouple.
[00:04:58] Carlos Mendez: tokenization differences earlier caused drift in some semantic search scores—how do you ensure consistent tokenization?
[00:05:03] Priya Gupta: we support the same tokenizers as the model checkpoints; when using different checkpoints we document tokenizer differences. as part of eval we normalize tokenization in the scorer so deltas are meaningful.
[00:05:13] Maya Chen: quick pause — any compliance questions?
[00:05:15] Devon Li: retention policies; we need logs for 1 year and ability to purge content on request.
[00:05:20] Priya Gupta: we can configure log retention and provide purge APIs for Private deployments; for Dedicated we have enterprise retention options. we'll include details in the security pack.
[00:05:29] Carlos Mendez: timeline — we'd like to pilot in Q4, two months to evaluate then plan prod in Q1. is that realistic?
[00:05:36] Maya Chen: yes that's a common timeline. first phase is sizing and benchmark (2-3 weeks), pilot (4-6 weeks), then production rollout.
[00:05:43] Jared Kim: who from Redwood will run the benchmarks?
[00:05:46] Liam O'Connor: SE-led with support from AE — we'll provide a reproducible benchmark repo and scripts (we'll include both vLLM/TGI and Redwood runtime comparisons).
[00:05:56] Anita Rao: can you show sample scripts?
[00:05:58] Liam O'Connor: yes we'll include sample run scripts and the benchmark sheet.
[00:06:02] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up—I'll send pricing and the Dedicated sizing worksheet after this call.
[00:06:08] Carlos Mendez: please also include security docs.
[00:06:10] Maya Chen: will do. any final questions?
[00:06:13] Devon Li: one quick one—how do you handle model rollouts and A/B tests?
[00:06:17] Priya Gupta: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B splits, automatic fallback, and per-model tracing so you can compare versions.
[00:06:25] Jared Kim: good. please add Jared to follow-ups.
[00:06:28] Maya Chen: noted. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with action items and schedule the benchmark.
[00:06:33] Carlos Mendez: thanks all.

Note: transcript has occasional transcription errors and speaker overlaps; timestamps approximate.
